findings.text: the first case asks for "a waiting run whose manifest carries the §1 shape of refused probe", but §2 explicitly makes that probe accepted ("the §1 probe, verbatim, is accepted as naming job 1306915"). Measured at HEAD 97eb0f321d: `_wait_probe_reference_kind(§1 probe)` returns `None`, so `_wait_probe_cannot_fail` (reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:800) refuses it and the run classifies `unreadable`; after §2's stated split of the `-c` string the same probe yields the words `squeue -h -j 1306915` and the reference kind measures `job`, so the probe is no longer refused and no run can carry the `unreadable` classification the case needs. Under the plan's own order (`f-abwrc-001`: "Build §2, then §4; §3 once …") the case is unbuildable; built before §2 it passes only while testing the pre-§2 refusal and turns red as soon as §2 lands. The fourth negative control inherits the same fate, since it asserts the refusal text on the same fixture

findings.reason: the deliverable needs one more clause naming `DUTY_ROW_FIELDS`; without it the implementer can pass the gate and still leave the new field unrequestable.
findings.text: the deliverable adds `detail` to `_live_item`'s projection (reckon/crew/obligations.py:727-736) but leaves out `DUTY_ROW_FIELDS` (reckon/crew/obligations.py:95-135), the vocabulary `project_run_rows` validates a narrowed request against at obligations.py:2018-2025. Its own docstring states the rule being broken: "A field whose value is empty is left off the row by the projection; a name is accepted here whether or not any duty of that kind is currently owed." With `detail` absent from the vocabulary, `crew view obligations --fields detail` is refused whenever no live duty happens to carry a non-empty detail, so the field the section exists to surface is requestable only in some fleet states, and the section's done-when cannot catch it because case 1 reads the item directly with no field selection
